markers.reason: asserts case-insensitive, backslash-folding filesystem semantics. On a case-SENSITIVE filesystem `sub/File.PY` and `sub/file.py` are genuinely different files, and `sub\file.py` is one filename containing a backslash - so NOT folding them is the correct answer there. normalize_lease_path is platform-sensitive by design (`leases.py`: `return text.casefold() if _CASE_INSENSITIVE_FS else text`); folding on Linux would manufacture FALSE lease collisions between distinct files and block legitimate concurrent work. Gated on the same constant the implementation reads, so the test and the code cannot disagree about which platform they are on.
